newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PNB sees trying year despite Q1 growth.
newsitem.headline: PNB sees trying year despite Q1 growth.

text.p: Philippine National Bank is expecting trying times ahead despite posting a slight profit growth in the first quarter of the year, bank officials said on Thursday.
The bank reported a 467 million peso net income in the first three months of this year against 340 million pesos in the same period last year.
The first quarter earnings did not include extraordinary items, although the bank sold foreclosed assets whose total book value amounted to 121 million pesos.

"1996 was a good year for us. And we can also say that the 1997 first quarter result is even more encouraging. But we are not telling you that 1997 would be an easy year for us," senior vice president Emerita Diaz said during an analysts' briefing.

"We are aware of the negative pressures of the economic environment in the banking industry -- the threat of competition, and thinning interest margin ... But the bank is determined to meet its targets. We are adopting the correct strategy to make this bank more profitable," she said.
Senior executive vice president Valentin Araneta said the bank is slowly and steadily regaining its footing after years of being dragged down by huge liabilities and a bloated bureaucracy.
Araneta said he expected the bank's loan portfolio, especially home mortgage and consumer loans, to grow despite concerns over rising bad debts in the banking industry.
"Despite the present scare, we would like to see our mortgage portfolio to grow, even double its present size," he said.
He assured analysts the bank has been prudent in giving out loans. Its past due ratio has declined to four percent by the end of March compared with five percent as of end-1996.
